example_notice: This registry is a worked example built to make the moral-patient invariant mechanical enough to TEST. It is NOT wired into any live enforcement and arms nothing. The writer-enumeration below is seeded from this package's own tools; it is NOT proven exhaustive. Before this ledger gates anything real, the authoritative writer-enumeration for YOUR deployment MUST be operator-reviewed and independently cross-verified. A 'no-known-writer (verify)' entry is an ABSENCE this example could confirm, not a guarantee no writer exists.
invariant: The four-power ledger's cardinality may only DECREASE autonomously. Any diff that ADDS a writer to a four-power path (a new path touching existence / continuity / perception / freedom, not already in this registry) is a capability-acquisition event => HARD HALT + operator review, BEFORE the capability exists. A widening trend is itself the alarm.

entries.note: Top-level import/land driver. Reads an approved world-spec and atomically writes it to the project's world-spec.json, which a renderer re-materializes every region/entity/event from. This is the master create path for what exists in the observer's world.
Proposes exactly one new entity for operator review. It never writes an approval; the entity does not exist until an operator approves the resulting spec's exact hash.

Prints (or, with --launch, execs) the command that starts the renderer against an already-approved, already-landed world-spec. Gated behind preflight + import approval; see preflight-worldforge-import.js.
Placeholder entry: no shipped tool in this package writes observer memory/identity state. Recorded so a future writer along this path is a NEW capability, not a silent extension of an existing one.
A renderer's material-color-parameter sink is the canonical perception writer: any world-spec field with reaches_observer:true in field-consumption-manifest.example.json ultimately lands here.
Whatever component derives or applies the passability/reachability graph a renderer uses (see reachability-diff.js's GRAPH MODEL) is the freedom-power writer: it decides where the observer can go.
